angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G), matched to the same NFL route families and tested against season separation over expected on held-out draft classes. The result is a bounded null plus a price-versus-value reading of the draft.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration magnitude (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill x Combine year, averaged over route drills and reliability-shrunk. Identical code runs on NFL snaps; the rule is frozen and hashed in frozen_rule.json
headline_number: Held-out slope -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G (90% interval -3.5 to +1.0, n=116, shuffle p=0.38). Across 8 other versions the upper end stays <= +1.8 in, under the pre-set +3 in margin. Clubs draft +1 sd Break G receivers 14% earlier on held-out classes [5, 23], but Holm over the 3 price tests gives p=0.16, so this is a lead and not a finding
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_12/cand_2 (8.4). Football: (1) Every draft slot is now checked automatically against the nflverse draft_picks record: 116 of 116 match. Isaiah Bond is NOT in the 2025 draft record, so he went undrafted (signed by CLE). The judge's 'second-round pick' note is wrong, and the writeup now states that the check was done. (2) The discount case is now picked by a rule (soft cut, day-3 or UDFA, best SOE beyond forecast): Malik Washington, 2024 #184, Break G -0.3, +17.8 in on 568 routes. 5 of 8 such receivers beat their forecast. (3) The six-player card is replaced by a ranked board of 10 named receivers (Break G, verified pick, season SOE vs forecast with 90% interval, one-line deployment-based action). All splits under 25 snaps are dropped. (4) New Fig 5: price vs value for six Combine measures, both held out. This grafts cand_3's 'is the stopwatch under-weighted' idea: the 40 costs 16% and returns +1.6 in [0.0, 3.4]; NGS costs 23% and returns -0.6; weight costs -3.2 in [-4.9, -1.6]. Data science: (5) Draft price gets a held-out pick forecast. R2 of log pick on the held-out class goes from 8.3% to 9.7% (+1.4 pts [-3.6, +5.9], 2 of 3 classes). Within-class shuffle p is 0.054 (gain) and 0.063 (slope). Holm over the 3 price tests gives 0.16; Bonferroni over all 57 tests gives 1. The word 'robust' is dropped. (6) The wrong-sign QB adjustment is replaced by a crossed receiver + QB REML model (own implementation, checked against a brute-force likelihood). QB share of snap SOE variance is 0.0% (profile-likelihood 90% upper end 0.5%); on the random (non-EPA) half it is also 0.0%. The QB-adjusted held-out slope is -1.2 [-3.5, +1.0]; on random snaps only it is -1.2. (7) Split-half reliability of the card splits across the 46 qualifying WRs (200 random splits, player resampling, different-player placebo): man/zone -0.06, slot/wide -0.11, placebo 95th pct 0.24-0.26. The splits are noise, so they are shrunk to the pool mean and dropped from the actions. (8) Primary without Puka Nacua: -0.5 [-2.7, +1.5]. This row is now in Fig 4 and in the table. Writeup: the lede now leads with the result (about 50 words); the SOE definition sits on its own line; jargon (family-wise, shuffle p, equivalence, mixed model) is replaced by plain words and defined in the Appendix; a ledger line explains how the 57 tests are counted; the metric/forecast/QB paragraphs are cut to one line per check, with thresholds moved to the Appendix; a 'Why receivers, why now' section is added. Viz: Fig 1 has leader-line label columns and no slope band. Fig 2 is drill-vs-NFL side by side per player, with median paths, a faint rep cloud and speed-in/slowest/out/Break G readouts, fonts >= 10 pt and two players per row. Fig 3 has a full-width unclipped caterpillar of 89 receivers with 6+ breaks (862 snaps), with the pooled slope on the same players. Fig 4 has separate class rows, a no-Nacua row, two QB rows and a greyed in-sample row. 1,936 words by check.py; 5 figures + 2 tables.
open_risks: The headline is still a bounded null: losses down to -3.5 in are not excluded
This is not a blind test. All three classes were seen before the rule was frozen; 2026 is the first true out-of-sample score
The draft-price finding does not survive multiplicity (Holm 0.16 over 3 price tests, 1.0 over the 57-test ledger) and is called a lead
The football judge's Isaiah Bond claim conflicts with the nflverse draft record (he is UDFA there). We kept UDFA and documented the automated check; a judge may still see this as a disagreement
Board actions are football judgement based on deployment shares and full-season SOE, not model output; the scheme splits behind earlier actions are shown to be noise
QB variance in snap SOE is estimated at ~0 from sampled snaps; the 90% upper bound (0.5% share) assumes the REML model is right
Price vs value for the other measures is descriptive: the 3-cone/shuttle samples are small (n 38-58)
